note: The fuzzer copies attacker-controlled bytes into a NUL-terminated rule buffer that is passed to the compiler.
The rule text is parsed into a regular-expression AST for a string declaration.
The AST is split into a head and remainder when a large ungreedy range-any node is present.
The split routine destroys the detached child node even though later parser logic can still revisit the chained AST state; the safety obligation is that the freed node must not remain reachable.
Later scan logic dereferences the chained string relationship; if the chain points through freed AST-derived state, this becomes the invalid read path observed by ASan.
